questions.q: In the Report Builder, what does the Fields pane show?
options: Only fields you have already added as columns
Every filter currently applied to the report
Every field the chosen report type exposes
A list of other reports in the same folder
questions.explain: The Fields pane lists every field available under the report's type, organized by object, ready to drag into the Outline.

questions.q: A custom report type relationship is set to "Accounts with or without Opportunities." What does that resemble in SQL?
options: An inner join, keeping only accounts that have opportunities
A UNION of accounts and opportunities
A subquery that counts opportunities per account
A left join, keeping every account whether or not it has an opportunity
questions.explain: "With or without" keeps the primary record even when no related record exists, the same way a left join does. "With" alone behaves like an inner join.

questions.q: What is a "block" in a joined report?
options: A filter applied to the whole report
A single row in the report
One report's worth of columns and filters, shown side by side with the others
A chart embedded in the report
questions.explain: Each block is effectively its own report (its own columns and filters, possibly its own report type), displayed alongside the other blocks in one joined view.

questions.q: What does the badge next to the word "Filters" in the Report Builder tell you?
options: How many columns the report has
How many filters are currently active
How many records matched the report type
Whether the report has been saved
questions.explain: That small numbered badge shows the count of active filters, letting you see at a glance how narrowed-down a report already is before looking at its results.

questions.q: What does a bucket column let you do?
options: Create a new custom field on the object
Merge two report types into one
Schedule a report to run automatically
Group existing field values into named categories within one report
questions.explain: A bucket column categorizes an existing field's values into buckets you name, entirely inside the report — no new object field required.

questions.q: Roughly how many rows does a Salesforce report display in the browser per run?
options: Unlimited — every matching record always renders
Up to 2,000 rows
Exactly 50 rows
It depends only on the user's license type
questions.explain: Reports display up to 2,000 rows in the browser. This protects rendering performance; export or the API is the path to the full underlying data set.

questions.q: Which export format keeps groupings, subtotals, and a chart image close to what's shown on screen?
options: Details Only (.csv)
Formatted Report (.xlsx)
Both formats preserve this equally
Neither format preserves any formatting
questions.explain: Formatted Report produces an .xlsx file that keeps the on-screen layout, including subtotals and a chart image. Details Only strips all of that into flat rows.

questions.q: What does the Edit Layout screen on a custom report type control?
options: Which fields are available to every report built on that report type
The color scheme of reports using that type
Which users can run the report type
The report's default chart type
questions.explain: Edit Layout sets the ceiling on available fields and sections for any report built on the type — it doesn't touch user access, which is controlled separately through folder sharing and permissions.

questions.q: A subscription has Attach File set to Formatted Report. What does a recipient receive?
options: A .csx details-only file
An .xlsx file they can open without logging into Salesforce
A live link that requires Salesforce login to view
Nothing; Attach File only applies to dashboards
questions.explain: Formatted Report delivers an .xlsx attachment. Report Details (.csx) is the alternative, details-only format — both let the recipient open the file without logging in.

questions.q: What actually controls who can see a given report?
options: A sharing checkbox on the report itself
The folder the report is saved in
The report type it was built from
The user's profile alone, regardless of folders
questions.explain: Reports don't carry their own sharing setting. Visibility is controlled by the folder a report is saved into and how that folder is shared.

questions.q: What makes a widget title like "Open Pipe This FQ" better than "Report 3"?
options: It's shorter in character count
It describes what the number actually tells a viewer, rather than just referencing the underlying report
It automatically changes the chart type
Salesforce requires widget titles to include a fiscal quarter
questions.explain: A good widget title communicates meaning at a glance. Naming a widget after what it tells a viewer — rather than an arbitrary report label — makes the dashboard self-explanatory.

questions.q: Why would a funnel chart be a good fit for a pipeline-by-stage dashboard component?
options: Funnels are required by Salesforce for all Opportunity reports
Funnels show a sequence with expected drop-off between stages, which matches how a pipeline narrows
Funnels are the only chart type that supports live previews
Funnels automatically calculate win rate without a source report
questions.explain: A funnel visually represents a sequence that's expected to narrow at each stage — exactly the shape of a sales pipeline moving from early to late stages.

questions.q: What access level does a viewer need to use a dashboard filter?
options: Manager access to the folder
Editor access to the dashboard
No special access beyond being able to view the dashboard already
System Administrator profile
questions.explain: Using a filter is a viewing-time convenience, not a configuration change — anyone who can already see the dashboard can use its filters without needing edit rights.

questions.q: What does a dashboard's "running user" determine?
options: Who is allowed to edit the dashboard
Whose record-level data access determines what shows up in the dashboard
Which folder the dashboard is saved in
How often the dashboard refreshes
questions.explain: The running user's data access is what actually produces the numbers and records shown. Everything displayed reflects what that person, specifically, is allowed to see.

questions.q: What controls who can see a given dashboard?
options: The dashboard's own private sharing checkbox
The folder the dashboard is saved in, same as reports
Whoever created the underlying reports
Dashboards are always visible to the entire org
questions.explain: Dashboards follow the same folder-based sharing model as reports — the folder's sharing settings determine the audience.

questions.q: Why does the lab add a dashboard filter on Owner instead of building a separate dashboard per rep?
options: Salesforce doesn't allow more than one dashboard per folder
A single dashboard filter lets any rep narrow the same dashboard to their own deals interactively
Filters are required before a dashboard can be saved
Owner filters are the only filter type Salesforce supports
questions.explain: A dashboard filter (Lesson 16) is the interactive, viewer-facing tool that lets one dashboard definition serve many people's individual views without duplicating the build.

questions.q: Why does case age matter on top of a simple open-case volume count?
options: Case age replaces the need for a Status field entirely
A case open for three weeks looks identical to one opened an hour ago on a pure volume report, hiding a real problem
Case age is only relevant for closed cases
Case age determines a case's report type automatically
questions.explain: Volume alone doesn't distinguish how long a case has been sitting. Case age is the field that surfaces cases that are stuck, the support equivalent of a stalled opportunity.

questions.q: Meridian's pipeline looked healthy at 3x coverage but the team kept missing quota. What did the days-in-stage report reveal?
options: The quota itself was set too high
A large share of the pipeline had been stuck in Proposal far past the normal cycle time
The report type was missing the Amount field
The sales team had stopped logging new opportunities
questions.explain: Total pipeline value alone didn't show that 40% of it had been stale in Proposal for over 60 days — well past Meridian's typical 21-day cycle. Days-in-stage was the report that exposed it.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four core questions pipeline reporting answers?
options: How much pipeline is open?
Is pipeline moving fast enough through stages?
What deals are at risk of stalling or missing close date?
What is the company's total headcount?
questions.explain: Headcount has nothing to do with pipeline health. The four core questions are: how much is open, is it enough, is it moving, and what's at risk.
